label: Temporal index, successive qualification, meta-time and explanatory regress
term: temporal index, successive qualification, meta-time and explanatory regress
resolution: The reported successive reply distinguishes predication at different reference positions from incompatible predication at one position. McTaggart argues that its explanation presupposes the A structure to be explained; a tensed or tenseless respondent must address that explanatory claim, rather than merely cite a well-typed index. Conversely, an added semantic argument does not by itself assert another objectively changing temporal series: that is part of the contested recurrence bridge. History.now is a designated index and History.IsAt is an assigned presence relation; neither establishes an objective moving present or metaphysical time. Causal edges, an unbounded past, epistemic reasons and object-language/metalinguistic hierarchies are separate relations. No verdict transfers among them without a defended mapping and adequacy norm. Existing motion-retorsion statements and their parked investigation are unchanged.
